ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: Fruit fly somatic cells have 4 pairs of chromosomes, of which No. 2, No. 3, and No. 4 are autosomes. It is known that the gene controlling the long-wing/vestigial-wing trait is located on chromosome No. 2, and the gene controlling the gray-body/ebony-body trait is located on chromosome No. 3. A group crossed an eyeless gray-body long-wing female fly with an eyed gray-body long-wing male fly. The phenotypes and proportions of the hybrid offspring are shown in the table. Answer the question: If the gene controlling the eyed/eyeless trait is located on chromosome No. 4, and gray-body long-wing eyed homozygotes are crossed with ebony-body vestigial-wing eyeless homozygotes, after the F1 intercross, how many phenotypes are there in both females and males in F2?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The table is grouped by “eyes” and “sex.” The left column shows that among the offspring, eyed account for 1/2 and eyeless account for 1/2; within the eyed and eyeless categories, the sex column shows females account for 1/2 and males account for 1/2. The header on the right is “gray body long wing : gray body vestigial wing : ebony body long wing : ebony body vestigial wing,” and the corresponding ratios for the four sex-and-eye-trait combinations are all 9:3:3:1. Reasoning: The stem states that the long-wing/vestigial-wing gene is located on autosome No. 2, and the gray-body/ebony-body gene is located on autosome No. 3; if the eyed/eyeless gene is located on autosome No. 4, then these three pairs of traits are located on different autosomes. Crossing gray-body long-wing eyed homozygotes with ebony-body vestigial-wing eyeless homozygotes makes F1 heterozygous for all three pairs of genes. When F1 intercross, the three pairs of genes are inherited independently, and each pair of traits has 2 phenotypes in F2, so the total number of phenotypes in F2 is 2×2×2=8. Since all three pairs of genes are on autosomes and are unrelated to sex, 8 phenotypes can appear in both female flies and male flies.
